name: project_path_doctor
purpose: Windows PATH auditor that reports dead entries, duplicates and shadowed executables, resolving machine and user PATH in true composition order.
notes: First Rust project on this machine, chosen as a workflow shakedown. Read-only by design: it reports, it never writes PATH. Born from real PATH shadowing hit during machine provisioning on 2026-09-15. Slice 1 is complete - registry reading and composition (winreg, chosen over the windows crate so the unsafe stays in the dependency), per-entry findings, executable enumeration with PATHEXT read from the environment, shadow resolution for both the running process and a fresh one, and the output layer with a versioned JSON contract in docs/SPEC.md. A GUI is a confirmed consumer, so the serialisation shape is defined once in pathdoc-core behind a serde feature rather than mirrored in the front end; it is at schemaVersion 3. Schema 2 replaced a conflicts-only shadows array with a full executables array after three of the four names worth reporting turned out to appear exactly once; schema 3 added live process positions after the tool was found to name the wrong winner for any name present in both a runtime-injected directory and a registry one. Exit 1 is reserved for actionable per-entry findings; shadowing is reported always and gates only under --fail-on-shadow. The acceptance test doubles as a drift canary for the machine's PATH and has caught two unannounced changes; volatile counts are isolated at the top of it. Registry access has been extracted into a winenv crate that knows nothing about PATH, so the planned env-var tool depends on it rather than on pathdoc-core: dependencies point from each tool at winenv, never from one tool at another. Decided: winenv stays in this repository, unpublished, and this repository becomes the toolkit workspace with the tools as members when the env-var tool exists - which bends the trunk's one-repo-per-project convention deliberately, for the trunk to amend when the restructure happens. Dual licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 with both licence files present, ready to publish. Tooling entry point is the justfile - just check runs fmt, clippy in both feature configurations, nextest and cargo-deny. Next is the roadmap: shell alias masking, decoding WindowsApps stubs, the env-var backup/diff tool, and an automated shadowing cross-check against Get-Command.
